wordpress.intro: Running your site on WordPress? The Avably Booking plugin adds your catalog, an availability calendar and a reservation form to it. Orders land right here, in the panel.
wordpress.step1Body: Use the form above — name the key so you know where it runs (e.g. “WordPress — company site”). We show the key exactly once, so copy it straight away.
wordpress.step1DoneBody: You already have an active key. If you did not save it, generate a new one above — the old one cannot be read again, and you can revoke whichever you no longer need.
wordpress.step2Title: Install the plugin on your site
wordpress.step2Body: Download the plugin package, then in your WordPress admin go to Plugins → Add Plugin → Upload Plugin and upload the .zip file. The plugin requires WordPress 6.5 or newer and PHP 8.1 or newer.
wordpress.step2Activate: After uploading, click “Install Now” and then “Activate Plugin” — until it is activated nothing shows up on your site yet.
wordpress.step3Title: Paste the key and place booking on a page
wordpress.step3Body: In WordPress open Settings → Avably Booking and paste the key into the “API key” field. You can leave the API URL at its default, or paste exactly the base address from the “Public reservations API” section above — both work. Then add the “Avably Booking” block to a page, or this shortcode:
wordpress.step3Hint: That's it — open that page as a customer and check that your equipment shows up. The first reservation will appear under Orders.
wordpress.troubleKeyBody: The key is invalid or has been revoked. Generate a new one above and paste it again in the plugin settings — make sure you copy the whole value, including the “avbl_” prefix.
wordpress.troubleSuspendedBody: Your account is not accepting new reservations right now — usually a billing matter. Check the Organization tab; the store resumes as soon as it is settled.
wordpress.troubleCacheTitle: The page shows stale data or an empty catalog
wordpress.troubleCacheBody: That is usually the WordPress cache. Clear it in your caching plugin and reload the page. The plugin disables caching on booking pages by itself, but catalog changes can take up to a minute.

embed.title: Embed bookings on your website
embed.intro: One snippet to paste on any website — Wix, Squarespace, WordPress without the plugin, or a hand-written page. The availability calendar and booking form work straight away, with no configuration.
embed.step1Body: This is the whole configuration. The snippet points at your store address, so there is nothing to fill in.
embed.step2Body: Paste the snippet where the booking form should appear. In website builders look for a block called “HTML code” or “Embed”.
embed.step2Hint: The booking form appears exactly where you paste it and adjusts its height to the content.
embed.step3Body: The preview shows exactly the same view your customer will see.
embed.optionProduct: Pins the widget to a single item (its catalogue identifier). Without it the customer picks an item from the list.
embed.optionLang: Forces the widget language: pl or en. Without it the widget uses the store language.
embed.optionTheme: Light or dark theme. Without it the widget is light.
embed.safetyBody: The snippet contains no key and no password — you can paste it on any page and show it to anyone. The booking form runs in a separate frame on our server, so the data your customer enters is not accessible to the page hosting the widget.

organization.title: Organization
organization.description: Organization details shown on documents and in billing.
organization.name: Name
organization.readOnly: This screen is read-only. Avably support applies changes to organization data.
organization.apiKeysDescription: API keys for external integrations — catalog, availability and reservations on your own website.
organization.dataExportDescription: Download orders, customers and the catalog as CSV files — your data belongs to you.
organization.customFieldsDescription: Extra data on customers, orders and products — the fields the standard form does not cover.

paymentSettings.title: Payments
paymentSettings.intro: Online payments in your store are handled by an external provider. You open an account there, pass verification, and your customers' money goes straight to your account — we only act as an intermediary.

stageHint.missing: You do not have a payment account yet. Without one, the store offers bank transfer and payment on delivery only.
stageHint.pending: The account exists, but the provider has not cleared it to accept payments yet.
stageHint.payouts_blocked: The account accepts payments, but payouts are on hold — the money stays with the provider until you unblock it.
stageHint.ready: The account accepts payments and pays out funds.

paymentSettings.refreshOk: Account state read from the provider.
paymentSettings.refreshFailed: Could not read the account state:
paymentSettings.unavailable: Online payments are temporarily unavailable on the platform side. We are working on it — no action is needed from you.
paymentSettings.ownerOnly: Only the organisation owner can connect a payment account.
paymentSettings.requirementsHint: The names come from the provider — you fill them in on their form via “Finish verification”.

suspendedOrganization.title: Organization suspended
suspendedOrganization.description: Access to the panel has been put on hold. Contact Avably support to restore access.

accessRevoked.title: Access revoked
accessRevoked.description: You no longer have access to this organization. Sign in again to continue — if you belong to another organization, it will be selected automatically.

dataExport.intro: Download your data as CSV files (UTF-8, semicolon separator — they open directly in Excel). Amounts are stored in grosze, with the order currency in a separate column.
dataExport.errorLimit: The export exceeds the limit of 10,000 rows. Narrow the date range and try again.
dataExport.errorRange: Invalid date range. Use the YYYY-MM-DD format (the start date must not be later than the end date).

orders.title: Orders
orders.description: Number, order and payment statuses, rental period, customer, amounts in grosze with the row currency, and delivery and payment methods. The date range filters by rental start date.

customers.title: Customers
customers.description: Contact details, invoice details and order counts. This is a full dump of your customers' personal data — available to the organization owner only.
customers.ownerOnly: Only the organization owner can download the customers export.

catalog.title: Catalog
catalog.description: Products with prices, deposits and pricing tiers. Each row is a product with one tier — a format prepared for future import.

customFields.title: Custom fields
customFields.intro: Add the data that the standard form does not cover — licence number, meter reading, whatever you keep in a spreadsheet today — to customers, orders and products.
customFields.readOnly: Custom fields are managed by the organisation owner. Here you can see how they are set up.
customFields.emptyEntity: No fields for this kind of data yet.

form.label: Field name
form.lockedHint: This field already has saved data, so its kind and assignment cannot be changed. Archive it and create a new one if you need a different kind.

values.notSaved: The order was created, but its custom fields were not saved. Fill them in below.

issue.unknownDefinition: This field is not among the custom fields for this data.
issue.archived: This field is archived — its saved value can no longer be changed.
issue.hidden: This field is not shown in the panel, so it cannot be changed here.
issue.type: The value does not match the type of this field.
issue.controlChars: The value contains characters that cannot be saved.
issue.option: Choose one of the list entries.
issue.phone: Enter a phone number — 6 to 15 digits.
issue.range: The number is outside the allowed range.
issue.tooLarge: The custom fields together take up too much space — shorten the entries.
